title: Corneal & Ocular Surface Mastery: The Definitive Clinical Compendium
summary: An exhaustive visual guide to corneal ectasia, dystrophies, infections, and surgical management. This poster integrates hyperacute trauma protocols, advanced diagnostic staining, and keratoplasty survival strategies for the front-line ophthalmologist.

sections.title: Hyperacute Chemical Injury Management
content: Step 1: Immediate Profuse Irrigation: Use saline or Ringer’s lactate for at least 30 minutes until pH is neutral (7.0–7.2). Use Litmus paper to verify.
Step 2: Fornix Sweep: Use cotton-tipped applicator to remove retained particulate matter (especially in alkali burns like Sodium Hydroxide).
Step 3: Clinical Grading: Assess limbal ischemia (blanching). 100% involvement = Roper-Hall Grade IV (Very poor prognosis).
Step 4: Medical Inhibition: Topical steroids (first 7–10 days only to avoid melting), topical antibiotics, and cycloplegics.
Step 5: Systemic Support: Oral Vitamin C (ascorbate) and oral tetracyclines/Doxycycline to inhibit matrix metalloproteinases.
Step 6: Surgical Intervention: Acute phase Amniotic Membrane Transplantation (AMT) or chronic Limbal Stem Cell Transplantation (SLET/LSCT).

sections.title: Recurrent Corneal Erosion (RCE) in Lattice Dystrophy
content: Pathogenesis: Irregular epithelial adhesion over anterior stromal amyloid deposits.
Presentation: Acute, severe eye pain upon waking.
Conservative Therapy: Lubricating agents, hyperosmotic drops, and Bandage Contact Lenses (BCL).
Surgical Options: Phototherapeutic Keratectomy (PTK) to ablate superficial irregularities.
Graft Choice: Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty (DALK) preferred if endothelium is healthy; otherwise PKP.

branches: Acanthamoeba: Ring-shaped ulcer, pain out of proportion, IVCM (cysts), Biguanides/Diamidines.
Fungal: Feathery edges, satellite lesions, endothelial plaque, Sabouraud agar, Natamycin/Voriconazole.
Bacterial: Rapid progression (Pseudomonas in CL wearers), fortified antibiotics (Vancomycin/Ceftazidime).
Viral (HSV): Dendritic ulcer with terminal bulbs, Disciform edema (immune), Acyclovir/Ganciclovir.

sections.title: Traumatic Globe Repair Protocols
content: Corneo-Scleral Tear: Apply FIRST suture at the limbus (anatomical landmark).
Suture Materials: 10-0 Nylon for cornea; 7-0 or 8-0 Nylon for sclera.
Exploration: Mandatory to look for posterior extent of tear (may require disinserting EOMs).
IOFB Suspicion: Urgent CT Scan (1mm sections). MRI contraindicated if metallic.
Loose Sutures: Confirm via Seidel Test (fluorescein); remove to prevent infection/vascularization.

sections.title: Pseudophakic Bullous Keratopathy (PBK)
content: Definition: Endothelial decompensation following cataract surgery.
Clinical Signs: Diffuse stromal edema, epithelial bullae, Descemet's folds.
Risk Factors: Complicated ECCE/ICCE, large superior wounds, iris loss.
Surgical Goals: Restore clarity via EK (DMEK/DSAEK) if scarring is minimal, or PKP if full-thickness scar.
IOL Strategy: Combined procedure or staged (graft first, IOL later) for refractive predictability.

sections.title: Dry Eye Disease (DED) Diagnostics
content: Vital Stains: Rose Bengal (damaged epithelium), Lissamine Green, Fluorescein.
Functional Tests: Tear Break-Up Time (TFBUT), Schirmer test (1 & 2), Tear meniscus height.
Systemic Link: Check for Rheumatoid Arthritis (Swan neck/Boutonniere deformities) = Secondary Sjogren's.
Management: Environment modification, artificial tears (preservative-free), Cyclosporine, Punctal plugs.
Systemic Treatment: Oral Doxycycline for Meibomian Gland Dysfunction (MGD).

sections.title: Corneal Emergencies & Red Flags
content: Perforated Corneal Ulcer: AVOID digital manometry/tonometry (risk of extrusion).
Lagophthalmos: Risk of severe exposure keratopathy; needs moisture chambers or tarsorrhaphy.
Loose Suture post-PKP: Potential nidus for endophthalmitis; manage with BCL or removal.
Iris Transillumination in Trauma: Highly suggestive of a retained Intraocular Foreign Body (IOFB).
Topical Steroids in Alkali Burns: Limit to first 7-10 days to prevent collagenase-induced melting.

sections.title: Special Corneal Entities
sections.content:
Limbal Dermoid: A choristoma (normal tissue in abnormal site) containing hair/keratin. Associated with Goldenhar Syndrome (vertebral/cardiac anomalies). Management involves excision + LSCT if cosmetic/visual axis issues arise. 

ICE Syndrome: Characterized by abnormal endothelium migrating over the angle and iris. Presents with 'hammered silver' appearance, corectopia, and secondary glaucoma. 

Band Keratopathy: Deposition of calcium salts in Bowman’s layer. Causes: JIA, chronic uveitis, Silicone Oil contact, or systemic hypercalcemia. Manage with EDTA chelation.

content.explanation: Double-Shell/Soft-Shell Technique: Use dispersive viscoelastic to coat/protect the endothelium and cohesive viscoelastic to maintain AC space. Critical in FED, PBK, and post-PKP eyes.
